objects.description: Enumeration of the concrete JSON value types used by Jansson. Values identify whether a json_t instance is an object, array, string, integer, real (double), boolean true/false, or null.

Opaque-ish JSON value handle for all JSON types. Contains a type tag and a reference count. Instances are constructed via json_object(), json_array(), json_string*(), json_integer(), json_real(), json_true(), json_false(), and json_null(), and are reference-counted; use json_incref/json_decref to manage lifetime. The json_delete() function is the destructor invoked when the refcount reaches zero (do not call directly unless managing refcounts manually).

objects.definition:
#ifndef JANSSON_USING_CMAKE /* disabled if using cmake */
#if JSON_INTEGER_IS_LONG_LONG
#ifdef _WIN32
#define JSON_INTEGER_FORMAT "I64d"
#else
#define JSON_INTEGER_FORMAT "lld"
#endif
typedef long long json_int_t;
#else
#define JSON_INTEGER_FORMAT "ld"
typedef long json_int_t;
#endif /* JSON_INTEGER_IS_LONG_LONG */
#endif
objects.description: Integer type used by Jansson for JSON integers. In this header, when not using CMake’s generated config, it typedefs to long long (or long) depending on configuration macros. Use json_integer() and json_integer_value() to construct and read. Note: When JANSSON_USING_CMAKE is defined (as in the provided jansson_config.h), json_int_t is defined there instead; this typedef block is disabled.

Holds details about a parsing or packing error: line/column/byte position, a short source tag, and a fixed-size message buffer. Used with json_load* and json_pack_ex/json_vpack_ex to receive diagnostics.

objects.definition:
enum json_error_code {
    json_error_unknown,
    json_error_out_of_memory,
    json_error_stack_overflow,
    json_error_cannot_open_file,
    json_error_invalid_argument,
    json_error_invalid_utf8,
    json_error_premature_end_of_input,
    json_error_end_of_input_expected,
    json_error_invalid_syntax,
    json_error_invalid_format,
    json_error_wrong_type,
    json_error_null_character,
    json_error_null_value,
    json_error_null_byte_in_key,
    json_error_duplicate_key,
    json_error_numeric_overflow,
    json_error_item_not_found,
    json_error_index_out_of_range
};
objects.description: Enumeration of error codes returned via json_error_t->text sentinel and used by json_error_code(). Indicates the kind of failure encountered during JSON operations such as parsing or manipulation.

Function pointer type for supplying input to the parser via json_load_callback(). The callback should fill up to buflen bytes into buffer and return the number of bytes written; returning 0 indicates EOF.

objects.definition: typedef int (*json_dump_callback_t)(const char *buffer, size_t size, void *data);
objects.description: Function pointer type for receiving encoded JSON output with json_dump_callback(). The callback is invoked with chunks of size bytes and should return 0 on success; a nonzero value aborts dumping.
Function pointer type for custom allocation functions installed via json_set_alloc_funcs/json_set_alloc_funcs2.
Function pointer type for a custom reallocation function used with json_set_alloc_funcs2/json_get_alloc_funcs2.
Function pointer type for custom free functions installed via json_set_alloc_funcs/json_set_alloc_funcs2.

functions.name: json_object
functions.description: Create a new empty JSON object (dictionary/map). Returns a new reference to a json_t of type JSON_OBJECT.
requirements: Caller must decref the returned json_t when no longer needed to avoid leaks.

functions.name: json_array
functions.description: Create a new empty JSON array. Returns a new reference to a json_t of type JSON_ARRAY.
requirements: Caller must decref the returned json_t when no longer needed.

functions.name: json_string
functions.description: Create a new JSON string from a NUL-terminated UTF-8 string. Performs validation of the input string.
requirements: value should point to a UTF-8 encoded, NUL-terminated buffer.
Caller must decref the returned json_t when no longer needed.

functions.name: json_stringn
functions.description: Create a new JSON string from a buffer with explicit length. Intended for data that may include NUL bytes; performs validation.
requirements: value should point to a UTF-8 encoded buffer of at least len bytes.
len specifies the number of bytes to read from value.
Caller must decref the returned json_t when no longer needed.

functions.name: json_string_nocheck
functions.description: Create a new JSON string from a NUL-terminated buffer without validating UTF-8. Useful when input is known-valid or validation is undesired.
requirements: value should be NUL-terminated; no validation is performed.
Caller must decref the returned json_t when no longer needed.
Caller is responsible for ensuring the content is acceptable for downstream uses since UTF-8 is not checked.

functions.name: json_stringn_nocheck
functions.description: Create a new JSON string from a buffer with explicit length without validating UTF-8.
requirements: value should point to a buffer of at least len bytes; no validation is performed.
len specifies the number of bytes to read from value.
Caller must decref the returned json_t when no longer needed.

functions.name: json_integer
functions.description: Create a new JSON integer from the provided value.
requirements: Caller must decref the returned json_t when no longer needed.

functions.name: json_real
functions.description: Create a new JSON real (floating-point) number from the provided value.
requirements: Caller must decref the returned json_t when no longer needed.

functions.name: json_true
functions.description: Return the canonical JSON true value.
requirements: Caller may decref when done (standard reference-counted json_t semantics).

functions.name: json_false
functions.description: Return the canonical JSON false value.
requirements: Caller may decref when done (standard reference-counted json_t semantics).

functions.name: json_null
functions.description: Return the canonical JSON null value.
requirements: Caller may decref when done (standard reference-counted json_t semantics).

functions.name: json_incref
functions.description: Increment the reference count of a json_t and return the same pointer. No-op for immortal values (refcount == (size_t)-1).
requirements: json may be NULL; if non-NULL it must point to a valid json_t.

functions.name: json_delete
functions.description: Free a json_t and its contents immediately (do not call directly if using reference counting helpers). Normally invoked via json_decref when the refcount reaches zero.
requirements: json must be a valid json_t or NULL.
Do not call on values with immortal refcount ((size_t)-1).

functions.name: json_decref
functions.description: Decrement the reference count of a json_t and delete it when the count reaches zero. No-op for NULL or immortal values.
requirements: json may be NULL; if non-NULL it must be a valid json_t.

functions.name: json_decrefp
functions.description: Scoped/cleanup helper: decrefs the json_t pointed to by *json and then sets the pointer to NULL. Available when compiling with GCC/Clang.
requirements: json may be NULL; if non-NULL it must point to a json_t* variable.
After the call, *json is set to NULL.

functions.name: json_error_code
functions.signature: static inline enum json_error_code json_error_code(const json_error_t *e);
functions.description: Extract the error code from a json_error_t previously filled by Jansson operations.
requirements: e must be a non-NULL pointer to a json_error_t that was initialized/populated by Jansson functions.

functions.name: json_object_seed
functions.description: Seed the internal hash used by JSON objects (affects key hashing and iteration order stability).
requirements: Call before creating/using objects if deterministic seeding is required; later calls affect subsequent operations.
seed is an implementation-defined integer used for hashing.

functions.name: json_object_size
functions.description: Return the number of key/value pairs in a JSON object.
requirements: object must be a valid json_t of type JSON_OBJECT.

functions.name: json_object_get
functions.description: Look up a key in a JSON object and return the associated value without modifying its refcount. Marked warn_unused_result.
requirements: object must be a valid JSON object.
key should be a NUL-terminated string.
Returned pointer is borrowed; incref if you need to hold it.

functions.name: json_object_getn
functions.signature: json_t *json_object_getn(const json_t *object, const char *key, size_t key_len);
functions.description: Look up a key in a JSON object using an explicit key length and return the associated value (borrowed reference). Marked warn_unused_result.
requirements: object must be a valid JSON object.
key should point to a buffer of at least key_len bytes.
Returned pointer is borrowed; incref if you need to hold it.

functions.name: json_object_set_new
functions.description: Set or replace a key in a JSON object with the given value. By naming convention, this function steals the reference to value on success.
requirements: object must be a valid JSON object.
key should be a NUL-terminated string.
value must be a valid json_t.
On success, caller must not decref value (ownership transferred); if the call fails, value is typically untouched (check return value).

functions.name: json_object_setn_new
functions.signature: int json_object_setn_new(json_t *object, const char *key, size_t key_len, json_t *value);
functions.description: Set or replace a key in a JSON object using an explicit key length. By naming convention, steals reference to value on success.
requirements: object must be a valid JSON object.
key should point to a buffer of at least key_len bytes.
value must be a valid json_t.
On success, do not decref value; incref beforehand if you need to retain it independently.

functions.name: json_object_set_new_nocheck
functions.description: Like json_object_set_new but skips validation of the key (e.g., UTF-8 checks). Steals reference to value on success by naming convention.
requirements: object must be a valid JSON object.
key should be a NUL-terminated string; no validation is performed.
value must be a valid json_t.
On success, caller must not decref value (ownership transferred).

functions.name: json_object_setn_new_nocheck
functions.signature: int json_object_setn_new_nocheck(json_t *object, const char *key, size_t key_len, json_t *value);
functions.description: Like json_object_setn_new but skips validation of the key; key length is provided explicitly. Steals reference to value on success by naming convention.
requirements: object must be a valid JSON object.
key must point to at least key_len bytes; no validation is performed.
value must be a valid json_t.

functions.name: json_object_del
functions.description: Remove a key (and its value) from a JSON object by NUL-terminated key.
requirements: object must be a valid JSON object.
key should be a NUL-terminated string.

functions.name: json_object_deln
functions.signature: int json_object_deln(json_t *object, const char *key, size_t key_len);
functions.description: Remove a key (and its value) from a JSON object using an explicit key length.
requirements: object must be a valid JSON object.
key must point to a buffer of at least key_len bytes.

functions.name: json_object_clear
functions.description: Remove all key/value pairs from a JSON object, leaving it empty.
requirements: object must be a valid JSON object.

functions.name: json_object_update
functions.description: Update object with all key/value pairs from other (shallow merge semantics).
requirements: object must be a valid JSON object.
other must be a valid JSON object.

functions.name: json_object_update_existing
functions.description: Update only the keys already present in object with values from other.
requirements: object must be a valid JSON object.
other must be a valid JSON object.

functions.name: json_object_update_missing
functions.description: Insert only keys that are missing in object from other.
requirements: object must be a valid JSON object.
other must be a valid JSON object.

functions.name: json_object_update_recursive
functions.description: Recursively merge other into object (nested objects are merged rather than replaced).
requirements: object must be a valid JSON object.
other must be a valid JSON object.

functions.name: json_object_iter
functions.description: Return an opaque iterator positioned at the first element of an object iteration, or NULL if empty.
requirements: object must be a valid JSON object.
The returned iterator is opaque and must only be used with the json_object_iter* API.

functions.name: json_object_iter_at
functions.description: Return an opaque iterator positioned at the given key, or NULL if not found.
requirements: object must be a valid JSON object.
key should be a NUL-terminated string.

functions.name: json_object_key_to_iter
functions.description: Convert a key string to the opaque iterator token used by the foreach-style macros. Intended for internal/iterator use.
requirements: key should be a NUL-terminated string.
Only use with the iterator API as demonstrated by provided macros.

functions.name: json_object_iter_next
functions.description: Advance an iterator to the next element and return it, or NULL when the end is reached.
requirements: object must be a valid JSON object.
iter must be an iterator previously obtained from json_object_iter* for the same object.

functions.name: json_object_iter_key
functions.description: Return the key at the iterator position as a NUL-terminated string.
requirements: iter must be a valid iterator obtained from json_object_iter*.

functions.name: json_object_iter_key_len
functions.description: Return the length of the key at the iterator position.
requirements: iter must be a valid iterator obtained from json_object_iter*.

functions.name: json_object_iter_value
functions.description: Return the value at the iterator position (borrowed reference).
requirements: iter must be a valid iterator obtained from json_object_iter*.
Returned pointer is borrowed; incref if you need to hold it beyond the object's lifetime.

functions.name: json_object_iter_set_new
functions.description: Replace the value at the iterator position with the provided value. By naming convention, steals reference to value on success.
requirements: object must be a valid JSON object.
iter must be a valid iterator for object.
value must be a valid json_t.
On success, caller must not decref value (ownership transferred).

functions.name: json_array_size
functions.description: Return the number of elements in a JSON array.
requirements: array must be a valid JSON array.

functions.name: json_array_get
functions.description: Return the element at the given index from a JSON array (borrowed reference). Marked warn_unused_result.
requirements: array must be a valid JSON array.
index must be within the array's bounds for retrieval.
Returned pointer is borrowed; incref if you need to hold it.

functions.name: json_array_set_new
functions.description: Replace the element at the given index with value. By naming convention, steals reference to value on success.
requirements: array must be a valid JSON array.
index must refer to an existing element for replacement.
value must be a valid json_t.
On success, do not decref value (ownership transferred).

functions.name: json_array_append_new
functions.description: Append a value to the end of the array. By naming convention, steals reference to value on success.
requirements: array must be a valid JSON array.
value must be a valid json_t.
On success, do not decref value (ownership transferred).

functions.name: json_array_insert_new
functions.description: Insert a value at the given index, shifting subsequent elements. By naming convention, steals reference to value on success.
requirements: array must be a valid JSON array.
index must be within a valid insertion range for the array.
value must be a valid json_t.

functions.name: json_array_remove
functions.description: Remove the element at the specified index from a JSON array.
requirements: array must be a valid JSON array.
index must be within the array's bounds.

functions.name: json_array_clear
functions.description: Remove all elements from a JSON array, leaving it empty.
requirements: array must be a valid JSON array.

functions.name: json_array_extend
functions.description: Append all elements from other to the end of array.
requirements: array must be a valid JSON array.
other must be a valid JSON array.

functions.name: json_string_value
functions.description: Return a pointer to the internal NUL-terminated string buffer of a JSON string value.
requirements: string must be a valid JSON string.
The returned pointer is valid as long as the json_t string is alive and not modified.

functions.name: json_string_length
functions.description: Return the length in bytes of a JSON string value.
requirements: string must be a valid JSON string.

functions.name: json_integer_value
functions.description: Return the integer value stored in a JSON integer.
requirements: integer must be a valid JSON integer.

functions.name: json_real_value
functions.description: Return the floating-point value stored in a JSON real.
requirements: real must be a valid JSON real.

functions.name: json_number_value
functions.description: Return the numeric value of a JSON number (integer or real) as a double.
requirements: json must be a valid JSON integer or real for meaningful results.

functions.name: json_string_set
functions.description: Replace a JSON string's contents with a new NUL-terminated UTF-8 string, validating input.
requirements: string must be a valid JSON string.
value should point to a UTF-8 encoded, NUL-terminated buffer.

functions.name: json_string_setn
functions.signature: int json_string_setn(json_t *string, const char *value, size_t len);
functions.description: Replace a JSON string's contents with data from a buffer of explicit length, validating input.
requirements: string must be a valid JSON string.
value should point to a UTF-8 encoded buffer of at least len bytes.
len specifies the number of bytes to read from value.

functions.name: json_string_set_nocheck
functions.description: Replace a JSON string's contents without validating the NUL-terminated input as UTF-8.
requirements: string must be a valid JSON string.
value should be a NUL-terminated buffer; no validation is performed.

functions.name: json_string_setn_nocheck
functions.signature: int json_string_setn_nocheck(json_t *string, const char *value, size_t len);
functions.description: Replace a JSON string's contents from a buffer with explicit length without UTF-8 validation.
requirements: string must be a valid JSON string.
value should point to a buffer of at least len bytes; no validation is performed.
len specifies the number of bytes to read.

functions.name: json_integer_set
functions.description: Set the value of a JSON integer.
requirements: integer must be a valid JSON integer.

functions.name: json_real_set
functions.description: Set the value of a JSON real (floating-point) number.
requirements: real must be a valid JSON real.

functions.name: json_pack
functions.description: Create JSON values according to a format string and arguments (variadic convenience). Returns a new json_t constructed per the format.
requirements: fmt must follow Jansson's pack format specification.
Arguments must match fmt.
Caller must decref the returned json_t when no longer needed.

functions.name: json_pack_ex
functions.description: Like json_pack but allows passing flags (e.g., JSON_VALIDATE_ONLY, JSON_STRICT) and an optional error output struct.
requirements: fmt must follow Jansson's pack format.
flags should be a bitwise OR of defined JSON_* pack flags.
If error is non-NULL, it must point to writable json_error_t storage.
Caller must decref the returned json_t when no longer needed.

functions.name: json_vpack_ex
functions.signature: json_t *json_vpack_ex(json_error_t *error, size_t flags, const char *fmt, va_list ap);
functions.description: va_list variant of json_pack_ex for building JSON from a format string and argument list.
requirements: ap must be a valid va_list matching fmt.
fmt must follow Jansson's pack format.
flags should be a bitwise OR of defined JSON_* pack flags.
If error is non-NULL, it must point to writable json_error_t storage.

functions.name: json_unpack
functions.description: Parse a json_t into C variables according to a format string (variadic). Returns 0 on success, nonzero on failure.
requirements: root must be a valid json_t matching the structure implied by fmt.
fmt must follow Jansson's unpack format.
Output arguments must match fmt and be valid pointers when required.
Check the return value for success (0) or failure.

functions.name: json_unpack_ex
functions.signature: int json_unpack_ex(json_t *root, json_error_t *error, size_t flags, const char *fmt, ...);
functions.description: Like json_unpack but with flags and optional error reporting.
requirements: root must be a valid json_t.
fmt must follow Jansson's unpack format.
flags should be a bitwise OR of JSON_VALIDATE_ONLY or JSON_STRICT, etc.
If error is non-NULL, it must point to writable json_error_t storage.
Check the return value; 0 indicates success.

functions.name: json_vunpack_ex
functions.signature: int json_vunpack_ex(json_t *root, json_error_t *error, size_t flags, const char *fmt, va_list ap);
functions.description: va_list variant of json_unpack_ex.
requirements: root must be a valid json_t.
ap must be a valid va_list matching fmt.
fmt must follow Jansson's unpack format.
If error is non-NULL, it must point to writable json_error_t storage.
Check return value for success (0).

functions.name: json_sprintf
functions.description: Create a JSON string using printf-style formatting and return it as a json_t string. Marked with printf format attributes.
requirements: fmt must be a valid printf-style format string.
Arguments must match fmt.
Caller must decref the returned json_t when no longer needed.

functions.name: json_vsprintf
functions.description: va_list variant of json_sprintf to produce a JSON string via printf-style formatting.
requirements: fmt must be a valid printf-style format string.
ap must be a valid va_list matching fmt.
Caller must decref the returned json_t when no longer needed.

functions.name: json_equal
functions.description: Compare two JSON values for equality (deep structural equality). Returns nonzero if equal, 0 otherwise.
requirements: value1 and value2 must be valid json_t pointers.

functions.name: json_copy
functions.description: Create a shallow copy of a JSON value. Container elements are not deep-copied.
requirements: value must be a valid json_t.
Caller must decref the returned json_t when no longer needed.

functions.name: json_deep_copy
functions.description: Create a deep copy of a JSON value, recursively duplicating containers and their contents.
requirements: value must be a valid json_t.
Caller must decref the returned json_t when no longer needed.

functions.name: json_loads
functions.description: Parse a NUL-terminated string containing JSON text into a json_t. Flags tweak parsing behavior. On error, returns NULL and may fill error.
requirements: input must be a NUL-terminated string containing JSON data.
flags should be a bitwise OR of JSON_REJECT_DUPLICATES, JSON_DISABLE_EOF_CHECK, JSON_DECODE_ANY, JSON_DECODE_INT_AS_REAL, JSON_ALLOW_NUL, etc.
If error is non-NULL, it must point to writable json_error_t storage.
Caller must decref the returned json_t when no longer needed.

functions.name: json_loadb
functions.signature: json_t *json_loadb(const char *buffer, size_t buflen, size_t flags, json_error_t *error);
functions.description: Parse JSON text from a buffer with explicit length.
requirements: buffer must point to at least buflen bytes of JSON data.
buflen specifies buffer length in bytes.
flags are as for json_loads.
If error is non-NULL, it must point to writable json_error_t storage.

functions.name: json_loadf
functions.description: Parse JSON text from a FILE* stream.
requirements: input must be a valid readable FILE* positioned at the start of JSON content.
flags are as for json_loads.
If error is non-NULL, it must point to writable json_error_t storage.

functions.name: json_loadfd
functions.description: Parse JSON text from a file descriptor.
requirements: input must be a valid readable file descriptor.
flags are as for json_loads.
If error is non-NULL, it must point to writable json_error_t storage.

functions.name: json_load_file
functions.description: Parse JSON text from a file at the specified path.
requirements: path must be a valid NUL-terminated file path to a readable file.
flags are as for json_loads.
If error is non-NULL, it must point to writable json_error_t storage.

functions.name: json_load_callback
functions.signature: json_t *json_load_callback(json_load_callback_t callback, void *data, size_t flags, json_error_t *error);
functions.description: Parse JSON using a user-provided read callback. The callback fills a buffer and returns the number of bytes read until EOF.
requirements: callback must be a function of type json_load_callback_t that reads into the provided buffer and returns bytes read.
data is passed through to the callback.
flags are as for json_loads.
If error is non-NULL, it must point to writable json_error_t storage.

functions.name: json_dumps
functions.description: Serialize a json_t to a newly allocated NUL-terminated string according to flags. Returns a malloc-allocated buffer.
requirements: json must be a valid json_t.
flags should be a bitwise OR of JSON_INDENT(n), JSON_COMPACT, JSON_ENSURE_ASCII, JSON_SORT_KEYS, JSON_PRESERVE_ORDER, JSON_ENCODE_ANY, JSON_ESCAPE_SLASH, JSON_REAL_PRECISION(n), JSON_EMBED, etc.
Caller must free the returned char* with the library's free function (or compatible free).

functions.name: json_dumpb
functions.signature: size_t json_dumpb(const json_t *json, char *buffer, size_t size, size_t flags);
functions.description: Serialize a json_t into a caller-provided buffer, writing at most size bytes, using flags.
requirements: json must be a valid json_t.
buffer must point to a writable memory region of at least size bytes (or may be NULL depending on usage).
flags are as for json_dumps.

functions.name: json_dumpf
functions.signature: int json_dumpf(const json_t *json, FILE *output, size_t flags);
functions.description: Serialize a json_t to a FILE* stream using flags.
requirements: json must be a valid json_t.
output must be a valid writable FILE*.
flags are as for json_dumps.

functions.name: json_dumpfd
functions.signature: int json_dumpfd(const json_t *json, int output, size_t flags);
functions.description: Serialize a json_t to a file descriptor using flags.
requirements: json must be a valid json_t.
output must be a valid writable file descriptor.
flags are as for json_dumps.

functions.name: json_dump_file
functions.signature: int json_dump_file(const json_t *json, const char *path, size_t flags);
functions.description: Serialize a json_t to a file at the given path using flags.
requirements: json must be a valid json_t.
path must be a valid NUL-terminated file path to a writable location.
flags are as for json_dumps.

functions.name: json_dump_callback
functions.signature: int json_dump_callback(const json_t *json, json_dump_callback_t callback, void *data, size_t flags);
functions.description: Serialize a json_t using a user-provided write callback that receives chunks of bytes.
requirements: json must be a valid json_t.
callback must be a function of type json_dump_callback_t that writes out the provided buffer.
data is passed through to the callback.
flags are as for json_dumps.

functions.name: json_set_alloc_funcs
functions.description: Override the library's allocation and free functions globally (malloc/free pair).
requirements: Should be called before creating/using JSON values to ensure consistent allocation behavior.
malloc_fn must be a function compatible with json_malloc_t.
free_fn must be a function compatible with json_free_t.

functions.name: json_get_alloc_funcs
functions.description: Retrieve the currently configured allocation and free functions (malloc/free pair).
requirements: malloc_fn and free_fn must be non-NULL pointers to receive function pointers.

functions.name: json_set_alloc_funcs2
functions.signature: void json_set_alloc_funcs2(json_malloc_t malloc_fn, json_realloc_t realloc_fn, json_free_t free_fn);
functions.description: Override the library's allocation, reallocation, and free functions globally.
requirements: Should be called before creating/using JSON values to ensure consistent allocation behavior.
malloc_fn, realloc_fn, and free_fn must be compatible with their respective typedefs.

functions.name: json_get_alloc_funcs2
functions.description: Retrieve the currently configured allocation, reallocation, and free functions.
requirements: malloc_fn, realloc_fn, and free_fn must be non-NULL pointers to receive function pointers.

functions.name: jansson_version_str
functions.description: Return the library version string (e.g., "2.14.1").

functions.name: jansson_version_cmp
functions.signature: int jansson_version_cmp(int major, int minor, int micro);
functions.description: Compare the supplied version triple to the library version. Returns <0, 0, or >0 similar to strcmp-style comparisons.
requirements: major, minor, and micro should be non-negative integers.

endpoints.name: json_object
json_array
json_string

import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# Target: Generate valid UTF-8 buffers for use with jansson json_stringn/json_string_setn
# Requirements:
# - Return bytes (<= 4096) that are valid UTF-8 for validating APIs
# - FUZZ harness will also select a length (0..len(buf)) so embedding NULs and multi-byte
#   sequences provides interesting truncations (including cutting inside code points when len chosen smaller).
# - Provide diverse content: ASCII, multi-byte UTF-8, edge scalars, combining marks, emojis, RTL, long runs,
#   surrogate avoidance, overlong avoidance, BOM presence, control chars allowed in JSON strings? Jansson validates
#   UTF-8 but permits NUL via explicit length with JSON_ALLOW_NUL pack flag; json_stringn validates UTF-8 but allows NUL bytes.
# Strategy:
# - Assemble a corpus of snippets that are valid UTF-8, including NUL bytes inside.
# - Randomly concatenate several snippets up to a random size cap (<= 2048 default).
# - Ensure overall length <= 4096.
# - Deterministic randomness via seed.

ASCII_PRINTABLE = [bytes([c]) for c in range(0x20, 0x7F)]  # space..~
ASCII_CONTROL = [b"\t", b"\n", b"\r", b"\f", b"\b"]

# Some interesting Unicode code points as UTF-8 bytes
def u(codepoint: int) -> bytes:
    return chr(codepoint).encode('utf-8')

UNICODE_SNIPPETS: List[bytes] = [
    u(0x00A0),        # NO-BREAK SPACE
    u(0x00A9),        # COPYRIGHT SIGN
    u(0x00AD),        # SOFT HYPHEN
    u(0x03A9),        # GREEK CAPITAL OMEGA
    u(0x0401),        # CYRILLIC IO
    u(0x05D0),        # HEBREW LETTER ALEF
    u(0x061C),        # ARABIC LETTER MARK
    u(0x0627),        # ARABIC ALEF
    u(0x0660),        # ARABIC-INDIC DIGIT ZERO
    u(0x070F),        # SYRIAC ABBREVIATION MARK
    u(0x200B),        # ZERO WIDTH SPACE
    u(0x200D),        # ZERO WIDTH JOINER
    u(0x2028),        # LINE SEPARATOR
    u(0x2029),        # PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR
    u(0x202E),        # RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE
    u(0x2060),        # WORD JOINER
    u(0x2066),        # LRI
    u(0x2067),        # RLI
    u(0x2068),        # FSI
    u(0x2069),        # PDI
    u(0x20AC),        # EURO SIGN
    u(0x2116),        # NUMERO SIGN
    u(0x2122),        # TRADE MARK SIGN
    u(0x221E),        # INFINITY
    u(0x2323),        # SMILE
    u(0x23CE),        # RETURN SYMBOL
    u(0x2424),        # SYMBOL FOR NEWLINE
    u(0x25B6),        # PLAY
    u(0x2603),        # SNOWMAN
    u(0x2615),        # HOT BEVERAGE
    u(0x2620),        # SKULL AND CROSSBONES
    u(0x263A),        # WHITE SMILING FACE
    u(0x2665),        # HEART SUIT
    u(0x2699),        # GEAR
    u(0x2705),        # WHITE HEAVY CHECK MARK
    u(0x2764),        # HEAVY BLACK HEART
    u(0x27A1),        # BLACK RIGHTWARDS ARROW
    u(0x2B1B),        # BLACK LARGE SQUARE
    u(0x2B50),        # WHITE MEDIUM STAR
    u(0x3030),        # WAVY DASH
    u(0x303D),        # PART ALTERNATION MARK
    u(0x30A2),        # KATAKANA LETTER A
    u(0x4E2D),        # CJK: middle/center
    u(0x65E5),        # CJK: sun/day
    u(0x672C),        # CJK: book/base
    u(0x1F37A),       # BEER MUG
    u(0x1F354),       # HAMBURGER
    u(0x1F680),       # ROCKET
    u(0x1F4A9),       # PILE OF POO
    u(0x1F600),       # GRINNING FACE
    u(0x1F602),       # FACE WITH TEARS OF JOY
    u(0x1F44D),       # THUMBS UP
    u(0x1F9D1),       # ADULT (for ZWJ sequences)
]

# Combining marks to test normalization/combining sequences
COMBINING = [u(cp) for cp in [0x0300, 0x0301, 0x0308, 0x0327, 0x20DD]]

# Regional indicators for flags
REGIONAL = [u(cp) for cp in range(0x1F1E6, 0x1F1FF + 1)]

# Common multi-codepoint sequences
SEQUENCE_SNIPPETS: List[bytes] = [
    b"\xEF\xBB\xBF",                 # UTF-8 BOM
    b"Caf\xC3\xA9",                  # Café
    b"\xE6\x97\xA5\xE6\x9C\xAC\xE4\xB8\xAD",  # 日本中
    ("A" + "\u0301").encode('utf-8'), # A + COMBINING ACUTE
    ("e" + "\u0308").encode('utf-8'), # e + diaeresis
    ("\u0915\u094D\u0937").encode('utf-8'), # Devanagari conjunct क्ष
    ("\u0BA4\u0BCD\u0BB0").encode('utf-8'),  # Tamil tr
    ("\u1100\u1161\u11A8").encode('utf-8'),  # Hangul jamo 각-like
    ("👩\u200D🚀").encode('utf-8'),          # woman ZWJ rocket
    ("👩\u200D💻").encode('utf-8'),          # woman technologist
    ("🇺🇸").encode('utf-8'),                 # US flag (RI pair)
    ("🏳\u200D🌈").encode('utf-8'),          # rainbow flag sequence
    ("مرحبا" ).encode('utf-8'),              # Arabic
    ("שלום" ).encode('utf-8'),               # Hebrew
]

# Include a NUL-including valid sequence chunk for json_stringn (explicit length)
NUL_CHUNKS = [
    b"ABC\x00DEF",            # embedded NUL in ASCII
    ("\u0000").encode('utf-8'),  # UTF-8 NUL is 0x00
]

# Quoted/backslash-heavy content to exercise escaping when dumping
ESCAPE_HEAVY = [
    b"\\\\\\\\",                       # lots of backslashes
    b"\"quote\" and backslash \\ mix",  # quotes and slashes
    b"/slashes/and\\backslashes\\/",   # slashes
]

# JSON-like structures as plain text (valid UTF-8) to interact with pack/unpack flows
JSON_LIKE = [
    b"{\"key\":\"value\"}",
    b"[1,2,3,\"x\"]",
    b"{\"nested\":{\"a\":1,\"b\":[true,false,null]}}".replace(b"true", b"true"),
]


def weighted_choice(rng: random.Random, items: List[Tuple[bytes, int]]) -> bytes:
    total = sum(w for _, w in items)
    x = rng.randrange(total)
    s = 0
    for b, w in items:
        s += w
        if x < s:
            return b
    return items[-1][0]


def random_codepoint_bytes(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Generate a valid UTF-8 sequence from selected ranges, excluding surrogates and beyond U+10FFFF
    ranges = [
        (0x0001, 0x007F),   # printable ASCII (exclude NUL here; handled elsewhere)
        (0x0080, 0x07FF),
        (0x0800, 0xD7FF),   # exclude surrogate block
        (0xE000, 0xFFFF),
        (0x10000, 0x10FFFF),
    ]
    lo, hi = rng.choice(ranges)
    cp = rng.randint(lo, hi)
    return u(cp)


def build_buffer(rng: random.Random, target_max: int) -> bytes:
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    # Create a header prefix sometimes
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        # Mix of ASCII and controls
        prefix_len = rng.randint(0, 32)
        p = bytearray()
        for _ in range(prefix_len):
            if rng.random() < 0.15:
                p += rng.choice(ASCII_CONTROL)
            else:
                p += rng.choice(ASCII_PRINTABLE)
        parts.append(bytes(p))

    # Optionally start with BOM for parser behaviors
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        parts.append(b"\xEF\xBB\xBF")

    # Main content: choose a strategy
    strategies = [
        "ascii_run", "unicode_snippets", "mixed", "json_like", "emoji_heavy",
        "combining_sequences", "regional_flags", "escape_heavy", "nul_mix",
    ]
    strategy = rng.choice(strategies)

    if strategy == "ascii_run":
        run_len = rng.randint(1, min(512, target_max // 2 + 1))
        parts.append(bytes(rng.choice(ASCII_PRINTABLE)[0] for _ in range(run_len)))
    elif strategy == "unicode_snippets":
        count = rng.randint(5, 60)
        for _ in range(count):
            parts.append(rng.choice(UNICODE_SNIPPETS))
    elif strategy == "mixed":
        count = rng.randint(10, 100)
        for _ in range(count):
            r = rng.random()
            if r < 0.4:
                parts.append(rng.choice(ASCII_PRINTABLE))
            elif r < 0.75:
                parts.append(random_codepoint_bytes(rng))
            else:
                parts.append(rng.choice(SEQUENCE_SNIPPETS))
    elif strategy == "json_like":
        # Concatenate JSON-like chunks with separators
        count = rng.randint(1, 5)
        for i in range(count):
            parts.append(rng.choice(JSON_LIKE))
            if i != count - 1:
                parts.append(b"\n")
    elif strategy == "emoji_heavy":
        count = rng.randint(5, 80)
        for _ in range(count):
            parts.append(rng.choice(UNICODE_SNIPPETS[-12:]))  # bias to emoji range items
    elif strategy == "combining_sequences":
        base_letters = [b"A", b"e", b"o", b"n", b"\xC3\xA9"]  # A, e, o, n, é
        count = rng.randint(10, 80)
        for _ in range(count):
            base = rng.choice(base_letters)
            k = rng.randint(1, 4)
            seq = base + b"".join(rng.choice(COMBINING) for _ in range(k))
            parts.append(seq)
    elif strategy == "regional_flags":
        count = rng.randint(2, 40)
        for _ in range(count):
            parts.append(rng.choice(REGIONAL) + rng.choice(REGIONAL))
            if rng.random() < 0.2:
                parts.append(b" ")
    elif strategy == "escape_heavy":
        count = rng.randint(3, 40)
        for _ in range(count):
            parts.append(rng.choice(ESCAPE_HEAVY))
            if rng.random() < 0.5:
                parts.append(b"\n")
    elif strategy == "nul_mix":
        count = rng.randint(2, 30)
        for _ in range(count):
            parts.append(rng.choice(NUL_CHUNKS))
            # Surround NUL chunks with valid UTF-8 multi-byte
            parts.append(rng.choice(UNICODE_SNIPPETS))

    # Optional trailer with sequence snippets
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 10)):
            parts.append(rng.choice(SEQUENCE_SNIPPETS))

    # Build and trim to limit
    buf = b"".join(parts)
    if len(buf) > target_max:
        buf = buf[:target_max]

    # Ensure valid UTF-8 prefix: if we accidentally cut within a multi-byte sequence, trim back
    # to the last valid boundary so json_stringn with full size is valid.
    buf = _trim_to_valid_utf8_prefix(buf)

    # Guarantee non-empty sometimes, but allow empty too
    if len(buf) == 0 and rng.random() < 0.7:
        buf = b"ok"

    return buf


def _trim_to_valid_utf8_prefix(b: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Walk from the end backwards to ensure last character is complete
    i = len(b)
    # Up to 3 bytes back can be continuation bytes
    back = 0
    while i > 0 and back < 3 and (b[i-1] & 0xC0) == 0x80:
        i -= 1
        back += 1
    if back == 0:
        return b
    # Now i is at a potential leading byte; validate from there to end
    try:
        b[i: ].decode('utf-8')
        return b
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        # drop the incomplete sequence
        return b[:i]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Random target size up to 2048 to leave room for harness-selected truncation, but cap at 4096
    max_len = rng.randint(16, 2048)
    buf = build_buffer(rng, max_len)
    # Final safety cap
    if len(buf) > 4096:
        buf = buf[:4096]
        buf = _trim_to_valid_utf8_prefix(buf)
    return buf

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator targets inputs consumed by FUZZ_PARAM_STR in stubs that call:
# - json_string_nocheck(s.c_str())
# - json_object_set_new_nocheck(..., key.c_str(), value)
# - json_string_set_nocheck(string, s.c_str())
#
# Therefore, we should return a NUL-terminated C-string buffer (bytes) that is
# interesting across usages as either a JSON string payload or an object key.
# Jansson "nocheck" variants accept arbitrary bytes, as long as they end with a NUL.
# We'll generate a mixture of:
# - printable ASCII
# - keys with structural characters (dots, slashes, spaces, unicode-like sequences)
# - bytes with embedded NUL candidates near the end (not allowed inside for C-string, so we avoid interior NULs)
# - long/short lengths, edge cases around powers of two
# - escape-heavy content and potential JSON-relevant tokens
# - high bytes (0x80-0xFF) to exercise non-UTF8 paths
#
# We limit size to <= 4096 bytes including terminator.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

ASCII_PRINTABLE = (
    [ord(c) for c in "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"] +
    [ord(c) for c in "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ"] +
    [ord(c) for c in "0123456789"] +
    [ord(c) for c in " _-./\\:;,@#%&*+?!=()[]{}<>\"'|"]
)

# Some interesting byte sequences (no NULs inside)
INTERESTING_SNIPPETS = [
    b"",  # empty string
    b"true",
    b"false",
    b"null",
    b"0",
    b"-1",
    b"1.0",
    b"NaN",
    b"Infinity",
    b"-Infinity",
    b"/dev/null",
    b"C:\\path\\to\\file",
    b"a.b.c",
    b"a[0]",
    b"key with spaces",
    b"emoji:\xf0\x9f\x98\x80",  # valid UTF-8 sequence
    b"badutf:\x80\x81\xfe\xff",  # invalid UTF-8 bytes
    b"quote:\" backslash:\\",
    b"newline\ncarriage\rtab\t",
    b"colon:comma,braces{}brackets[]",
    b"longkey_",
]

# Expand one snippet to various sizes by repetition
def build_from_snippet(rng: random.Random, base: bytes, target_len: int) -> bytes:
    if len(base) == 0:
        # fill with random printable/high bytes
        return rand_mixed_bytes(rng, target_len)
    out = bytearray()
    while len(out) < target_len:
        out.extend(base)
    return bytes(out[:target_len])

# Generate mixed bytes without NULs
def rand_mixed_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    for _ in range(n):
        mode = rng.randrange(4)
        if mode == 0:
            out.append(rng.choice(ASCII_PRINTABLE))
        elif mode == 1:
            # high byte non-UTF8 range
            out.append(rng.randrange(0x80, 0x100))
        elif mode == 2:
            # JSON structural characters
            out.append(rng.choice([ord(c) for c in '{}[]:,\"']))
        else:
            # whitespace variety excluding NUL
            out.append(rng.choice([9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 32]))
    return bytes(out)

def choose_lengths(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # Favor edge sizes but keep under MAX_TOTAL-1 (reserve for NUL)
    edges = [0, 1, 2, 3, 7, 15, 31, 63, 127, 255, 511, 1023, 2047, 3071]
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        L = rng.choice(edges)
    else:
        L = rng.randint(0, min(2048, MAX_TOTAL - 1))
    return min(L, MAX_TOTAL - 1)

def maybe_pathy(rng: random.Random, data: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Sometimes shape as a path-like or key-like string
    choice = rng.randrange(5)
    if choice == 0:
        parts = [b"usr", b"local", b"bin", b"etc", b"var", b"tmp", b"home", b"lib"]
        depth = rng.randint(1, 6)
        return b"/" + b"/".join(rng.choice(parts) for _ in range(depth))
    if choice == 1:
        # dotted key
        toks = [b"user", b"profile", b"name", b"id", b"settings", b"items", b"0", b"1"]
        depth = rng.randint(1, 6)
        return b".".join(rng.choice(toks) for _ in range(depth))
    if choice == 2:
        # bracketed path
        base = rng.choice([b"a", b"data", b"items", b"root"]) + b"[" + str(rng.randint(0, 50)).encode() + b"]"
        return base
    return data

def ensure_no_internal_nul(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Replace any accidental internal NULs (shouldn't occur, but be safe)
    if b"\x00" not in data:
        return data
    return data.replace(b"\x00", b" ")

def build_interesting_string(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Strategy selection
    strat = rng.randrange(7)
    maxlen = MAX_TOTAL - 1
    if strat == 0:
        # Pure ASCII printable small/edge size
        L = choose_lengths(rng)
        data = bytes(rng.choice(ASCII_PRINTABLE) for _ in range(L))
    elif strat == 1:
        # Mixed bytes including high bytes
        L = choose_lengths(rng)
        data = rand_mixed_bytes(rng, L)
    elif strat == 2:
        # From interesting snippet, possibly stretched
        base = rng.choice(INTERESTING_SNIPPETS)
        target = choose_lengths(rng)
        # Sometimes keep base as-is
        if rng.random() < 0.4 and len(base) <= maxlen:
            data = base[:maxlen]
        else:
            data = build_from_snippet(rng, base, target)
    elif strat == 3:
        # JSON-like content
        samples = [
            b"{\"a\":1}",
            b"[1,2,3]",
            b"\"string with spaces\"",
            b"{\"nested\":{\"x\":[true,false,null,123,4.56]}}",
            b"{\"dup\":1,\"dup\":2}",
        ]
        data = rng.choice(samples)
    elif strat == 4:
        # Long repeated pattern
        token = rng.choice([b"A", b"0", b" ", b"/", b"x", b"\xff", b"\x80"])  # avoid NUL
        L = choose_lengths(rng)
        data = token * L
    elif strat == 5:
        # Path-like or key-like
        base = rand_mixed_bytes(rng, rng.randint(1, 64))
        data = maybe_pathy(rng, base)
        if len(data) > maxlen:
            data = data[:maxlen]
    else:
        # Compose: prefix + snippet + suffix
        Lprefix = rng.randint(0, 32)
        Lsuffix = rng.randint(0, 32)
        prefix = rand_mixed_bytes(rng, Lprefix)
        mid = rng.choice(INTERESTING_SNIPPETS)
        suffix = rand_mixed_bytes(rng, Lsuffix)
        data = (prefix + mid + suffix)[:maxlen]

    data = ensure_no_internal_nul(data)

    # Occasionally trim or extend to boundary sizes
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        target = rng.choice([0, 1, 2, 3, 7, 15, 31, 63, 127, 255, 511, 1023])
        data = data[:target]

    return data


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Sometimes craft keys specifically interesting for object_set_new_nocheck
    special_keys: List[bytes] = [
        b"",  # empty key
        b"0",
        b"00",
        b"key",
        b"KEY",
        b"key\"quote",
        b"key\\slash",
        b"space key",
        b"leading space ",
        b" trailing space",
        b"dot.separated.path",
        b"brackets[0]",
        b"unicode:\xe2\x98\x83",  # snowman UTF-8
        b"badutf:\x80\xff",
        b"verylong_" + b"a" * 1000,
    ]

    if rng.random() < 0.35:
        data = rng.choice(special_keys)
    else:
        data = build_interesting_string(rng)

    # Ensure total size with NUL <= MAX_TOTAL
    data = data[: MAX_TOTAL - 1]

    # Append single NUL terminator for C-string usage
    return data + b"\x00"

import random
import struct
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets NUL-terminated C strings used as JSON object keys in Jansson APIs.
# The fuzz stubs request strings via FUZZ_PARAM_STR (and sometimes use _nocheck variants),
# so we produce a sequence of interesting, valid, NUL-terminated UTF-8 strings, including:
# - Empty and minimal keys
# - ASCII identifiers and mixed cases
# - Keys with whitespace, punctuation, JSON-escape characters
# - UTF-8 multi-byte sequences (BMP and beyond)
# - Long keys (but <= 4096 total buffer size)
# - Binary-like data including embedded NUL is NOT allowed here since FUZZ_PARAM_STR expects
#   a C string; therefore we avoid interior NULs and place a single NUL terminator between keys.
#
# The returned bytes buffer is a concatenation of multiple NUL-terminated strings so that the
# harness can consume them sequentially for multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

ASCII_BASE = [
    "",  # empty key
    "a",
    "A",
    "0",
    "_",
    "-",
    "key",
    "Key",
    "KEY",
    "true",
    "false",
    "null",
    "NaN",
    "Inf",
    "-Inf",
    "id",
    "name",
    "value",
    "long_key_name",
    "with space",
    "with\ttab",
    "with\nnewline",
    "with\rcarriage",
    "punctuation!@#$%^&*()[]{}<>,.?/~`|\\:",
    "json\\escape\\backslash",
    'quote"double',
    "apostrophe'",
    "slash/segment",
    ".dot.prefixed",
    "trailing-space ",
    " leading-space",
]

# Some valid UTF-8 examples (no interior NULs)
UNICODE_SAMPLES = [
    "π",           # Greek pi
    "你好",         # Chinese hello
    "こんにちは",     # Japanese
    "안녕하세요",       # Korean
    "Привет",       # Russian
    "👍",           # Emoji (U+1F44D)
    "𝒳𝒴𝒵",          # Mathematical script letters (surrogate pair in UTF-16)
    "café",         # Accented
    "mañana",       # Tilde
    "naïve",        # Diaeresis
    "résumé",
    "Ångström",
    "straße",
    "Crème brûlée",
]

HEX_CHARS = string.hexdigits.lower()
IDENT_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_"


def rand_ascii_ident(r: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=32) -> str:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    s = r.choice(string.ascii_letters + "_")
    s += "".join(r.choice(IDENT_CHARS) for _ in range(n - 1))
    return s


def rand_hexish(r: random.Random, min_len=2, max_len=40) -> str:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return "0x" + "".join(r.choice(HEX_CHARS) for _ in range(n))


def rand_path_like(r: random.Random, parts=3) -> str:
    segs = []
    for _ in range(parts):
        choice = r.randint(0, 3)
        if choice == 0:
            segs.append(rand_ascii_ident(r, 1, 10))
        elif choice == 1:
            segs.append(str(r.randint(0, 9999)))
        elif choice == 2:
            segs.append(r.choice(UNICODE_SAMPLES))
        else:
            segs.append(r.choice([".", "..", "-", "_", "@"]))
    return "/".join(segs)


def rand_float_str(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Strings that look numeric can affect object update/replace behavior via different keys
    forms = [
        lambda: str(r.randint(-2**53, 2**53)),
        lambda: f"{r.uniform(-1e9,1e9):.6f}",
        lambda: f"{r.random()}",
        lambda: f"{r.uniform(-1e-9,1e-9):.12e}",
        lambda: "-0",
        lambda: "+0",
    ]
    return r.choice(forms)()


def make_mixed_ascii(r: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=64) -> str:
    pool = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-./\\\t\n:\"'[]{}(),!@#$%^&*|~`?<>"
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Avoid interior NULs by not including \x00
    return "".join(r.choice(pool) for _ in range(n))


def ensure_terminated(s: str) -> bytes:
    # Encode as UTF-8 and append a single NUL terminator
    return s.encode('utf-8', 'strict') + b"\x00"


def assemble(strings: List[str]) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    for s in strings:
        chunk = ensure_terminated(s)
        if len(out) + len(chunk) > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        out.extend(chunk)
    # Guarantee at least one string (fallback to empty key) and within size
    if not out:
        out.extend(b"\x00")
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    strings: List[str] = []

    # Always include a small set of canonical cases first
    base = list(ASCII_BASE)
    r.shuffle(base)
    strings.extend(base[:r.randint(5, min(12, len(base)))])

    # Include several unicode-rich keys
    uni = list(UNICODE_SAMPLES)
    r.shuffle(uni)
    strings.extend(uni[:r.randint(3, min(8, len(uni)))])

    # Randomly generated identifiers and path-like keys
    for _ in range(r.randint(3, 8)):
        strings.append(rand_ascii_ident(r, 1, r.randint(4, 20)))
    for _ in range(r.randint(2, 6)):
        strings.append(rand_path_like(r, parts=r.randint(2, 5)))

    # Hex-ish and numeric-looking keys
    for _ in range(r.randint(2, 5)):
        strings.append(rand_hexish(r, 2, 24))
    for _ in range(r.randint(2, 5)):
        strings.append(rand_float_str(r))

    # Mixed ASCII including characters significant to JSON and iterators
    for _ in range(r.randint(3, 8)):
        strings.append(make_mixed_ascii(r, 1, r.randint(5, 40)))

    # Deliberately long keys (but overall buffer <= 4096)
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        long_len = r.randint(128, 512)
        strings.append(make_mixed_ascii(r, long_len, long_len))
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        # Long unicode by repeating a sample
        s = r.choice(UNICODE_SAMPLES) * r.randint(16, 64)
        strings.append(s)

    # Possibly duplicate some keys to exercise replace vs insert
    if r.random() < 0.8 and strings:
        dup_count = r.randint(2, 6)
        for _ in range(dup_count):
            strings.append(r.choice(strings))

    # Shuffle to diversify consumption order across FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls
    r.shuffle(strings)

    # Assemble into NUL-terminated sequence not exceeding MAX_TOTAL
    return assemble(strings)
